text.p: Apostolos Kaklamanis, proposed by the ruling socialist party, was re-elected president of parliament with 154 votes on the second ballot on Tuesday, parliament officials said.

Kaklamanis had failed to secure the necessary 151 votes in the first round earlier on Tuesday, getting one ballot short despite the fact 160 out of 162 socialist deputies were present in the 300-seat parliament during the vote.
A second round was hastily organised and 287 deputies cast their ballots. The conservative New Democracy candidate Anna Psarouda-Benaki got 94 votes from her party's 108 deputies.
Kaklamanis was first elected parliament president in 1993 when the socialists returned to power.
Three smaller parties cast blank ballots, bringing the number or blank or spoiled ballots to 39. --Dina Kyriakidou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
